summary: US-023c2: Catalog emits performance.published schema 5 for rule-enabled maps
description:
**Created during TKT-180's second ai-review**, which found ADR-041's rollout section self-contradictory: it argued that consumer-before-producer ordering *"is only expressible as separate merges"* and then assigned both inventory's schema-5 arm and catalog's emission to TKT-181.

**A shared merge does not order a deployment.** Catalog and inventory start independently, so one PR carrying both does not guarantee inventory is running first. If catalog emits while an old inventory replica is still up, that replica **quarantines the event, acks it, and latches unready** — and deploying the capable binary does **not** repair it. Quarantined originals were acked, so recovery is `reprocess-quarantine` **plus a restart**, by an operator. Newly published performances would have no inventory pool until someone notices.

So the producer gets its own revision.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Catalog emits `performance.published` **schema 5** for a seated performance whose bound seat-map version has `orphan_prevention_enabled` true, carrying the exact `seat_map_id` and the flag.
- [ ] A rule-**off** seated map still emits **schema 4**, byte-identical to today's golden. A GA performance is untouched.
- [ ] The schema-5 payload has its own golden, and the schema-4 golden is unchanged in the same commit — the pair is what proves the fork rather than a rewrite.
- [ ] The event carries the version the performance is bound to, never the family's current version (ADR-029) — a test seats a performance against v1, publishes v2 with a different setting, and asserts the emitted event still describes v1.
- [ ] Smoke proves an enabled map publishes at schema 5 and provisions an inventory pool **with** its adjacency projection (TKT-181's work, exercised end to end here for the first time).

### Two additions from TKT-180's third ai-review

**1. This ships AFTER the rule (TKT-182), not before it.** The original order put emission before enforcement, which opens a window where organizers have enabled the rule, inventory has recorded the flag and the projection, and buyers can still strand seats — silently, for the length of a deployment, on a revenue rule someone deliberately turned on. TKT-182 is dormant until a schema-5 pool exists, so shipping it first costs nothing.

**2. Performances already published against an enabled map must be re-emitted, and nothing else in the sequence does it.** TKT-179 shipped the setting before this ticket ships the transport, so a performance can be published against a rule-enabled map **today**: catalog emits it at schema 4, sets `event_emitted_at`, and never emits it again — re-POSTing publish is idempotent and will not re-fire. Inventory provisions an ordinary seated pool with no flag and no adjacency, and it stays that way for ever while the back office insists the rule is on.

- [ ] A correction wave re-emits `performance.published` at schema 5 for every published performance bound to a rule-enabled map version, under a **fresh event identity** — the existing `reemit-policies` path uses fixed correction ids that may already be in `consumed_events`, where a replay is a silent no-op.
- [ ] Inventory's schema-5 handler **upgrades an existing seated pool** — attaching the flag and projection to a pool that already exists — rather than assuming it only ever provisions new ones. (This may require an amendment to TKT-181's scope; check before starting.)
- [ ] The wave is replay-safe and idempotent, proven by running it twice.
- [ ] A test seeds a performance published against an enabled map *before* the wave and asserts it ends up with flag and projection.

**Deploy note:** TKT-181's inventory and TKT-182's rule must both be fully rolled out before this is enabled. That ordering is the whole reason this ticket exists.

Quality gates: `make check` green; both goldens; smoke.

reference.summary: The rollout rule this ticket enforces

governingAdrs.why: The producer half of the bump, and the reason it is a separate revision: bump on consumer semantics, and never emit a variant before every consumer accepts it.
The event must name the exact bound version, never the family's current one — resolving the family would describe a map the pool is not seated against.
Quarantine and readiness behaviour is what makes a premature emission expensive: quarantined originals are acked and recovery is manual.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
Carved out of TKT-181 during TKT-180's ai-review, to make ADR-041's own ordering claim true. Planning inherited from TKT-175.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
## Claimed — TKT-183

**Branch:** `TKT-183-catalog-schema5` off `origin/main` (which now contains TKT-182).

**Selection reason:** its only blocker, TKT-182, is merged. It is the last ticket of the ADR-041 sequence and the one the whole ordering argument exists for — the producer gets its own revision precisely so the enforcer is already deployed when the first schema-5 event is emitted.

**Gate waiver (recorded per the run directive).** The repo owner waived all four human gates for this autonomous run as a process experiment. Gates 1, 2, 3 and 4 are self-performed: priority given, plan decisions resolved by me against the cross-model critique, merge self-performed after the review guide is posted, and COS self-validated against test evidence on merged code. This ticket ran **gateless**, deliberately.

**Board discipline correction.** TKT-182 was merged with no claim, plan, plan-final or ai-review comment on the board — the trail was written only at the end. That gap is recorded in TKT-182's closeout and was **not** backfilled. This ticket posts each marker comment at its stage, as the pipeline requires.

**Governing ADRs, re-resolved against `docs/adr/` at claim time** (not the shaping-time snapshot):

- **ADR-041** — the decision this ticket completes. Fixes the emission rules: schema 5 carries the exact `seat_map_id` + flag; rule-off maps stay byte-identical at schema 4; the correction wave needs a **fresh, deterministic-per-performance** event identity and must not race catalog's own rolling deployment.
- **ADR-017** — schema evolution. §5b′: consumers dispatch on `schema` before decoding `data`. This ticket is the producer side of that contract, and the bump is justified on consumer semantics: schema 5 means "this pool needs an adjacency projection", which is a new required effect, not a new field.
- **ADR-029** — published seat-map versions are immutable and a performance is bound to **one** version. The event must describe the bound version, never the family's current one.
- **ADR-018** — catalog slot transitions decide under a row lock and emit **after** commit. The correction wave is not a transition, but it writes emission state and must respect the same ordering.
- **ADR-022** — migrations out-of-band, via each binary's `migrate` subcommand as a one-shot Compose job.
- **ADR-028** — response drift fails closed.
- **ADR-021** — name the adversary before claiming a guarantee. Relevant to any "every affected performance was corrected" claim the wave makes.

**Open question to resolve at plan time:** whether inventory's schema-5 handler already upgrades an existing seated pool, or whether TKT-181 only ever provisions new ones. The ticket flags this as possibly needing an amendment to TKT-181's scope — it is the first thing the plan must check against the real code, because the correction wave is worthless if the handler short-circuits on an existing pool.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
## Plan draft — TKT-183 (drafted by **gpt-5.6-sol**, effort high, read-only)

## 1. Definition of Done

TKT-183 is done when:

- A seated `store.Performance` is hydrated with `orphan_prevention_enabled` from its exact `performances.seat_map_id` row.
- `performancePublishedEnvelopeWithID` emits:
  - schema 5 with `seat_map_id` and `"orphan_prevention_enabled":true` for an enabled bound version;
  - the current byte-identical schema-4 payload for a rule-off seated version;
  - unchanged schemas 2 and 3 for GA and grouped festival slots.
- The existing schema-4 golden is unchanged and a new schema-5 golden is committed beside it.
- A real-stack test binds a performance to enabled v1, creates published v2 with the rule off, publishes the performance, and proves both the event and inventory projection describe v1.
- A correction command emits schema 5 for every historical candidate, with an identity distinct from both `EventID` and `BackfillEventID`, deterministic for that performance/publication.
- Correction progress is stored only after JetStream acknowledges publication. Crashes, concurrent commands, and reruns converge safely.
- The correction command is run only after all schema-4-producing catalog replicas have drained.
- A real-stack historical-state test starts with a schema-4 seated pool, runs the correction command twice, and ends with one rule-enabled pool and the exact adjacency projection.
- `make check` passes. No browser submission is required because no web write form changes.
- The guarantee is described as honest-writer/deployment consistency, not tamper-evidence.

## 2. Files to touch

| File | Planned change |
|---|---|
| [store.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/store.go) | Add a new `Performance.OrphanPreventionEnabled bool` field, explicitly documented as belonging to the exact bound seat-map version. |
| [postgres.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/postgres.go) | Extend existing `performanceColumns`, `performanceFrom`, and `scanPerformance` with a `LEFT JOIN seat_maps` on `sm.id = p.seat_map_id` and `COALESCE(sm.orphan_prevention_enabled,false)`. Add the correction-candidate list and marker methods. Make `MarkPerformanceEventEmitted` also mark schema-5 coverage when the exact bound map is enabled. |
| `services/catalog/internal/store/migrations/0015_performance_orphan_prevention_emission.sql` — **new** | Add nullable `performances.orphan_prevention_emitted_at`. This distinguishes old replicas—which only set `event_emitted_at`—from the new producer, and gives the wave durable convergence state. No index: this is a bounded one-shot full reconciliation, not a hot read. |
| `services/catalog/internal/store/orphan_correction_smoke_test.go` — **new** | Exercise the real Postgres candidate predicate, exact-version join, pagination, exclusions, and mark-after-publication state. |
| [events.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/events/events.go) | Add `OrphanPreventionEnabled bool` with `omitempty` to `PerformancePublishedData`; select schema 5 only for seated+enabled; fail closed on an enabled flag without a seat map. Add a distinct correction identity/publisher. Do **not** bump `backfillEpoch`. |
| [events_test.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/events/events_test.go) | Add schema-selection, payload, corrupt-combination, and correction-ID tests. |
| [wire_compat_test.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/events/wire_compat_test.go) | Add the schema-5 inline golden while leaving `TestWireGoldenPerformancePublishedSchema4Seated` literally unchanged. |
| `services/catalog/cmd/catalog/reemit_orphan_prevention.go` — **new** | Implement the injectable correction runner and `reemit-orphan-prevention` CLI command. |
| `services/catalog/cmd/catalog/reemit_orphan_prevention_test.go` — **new** | Test batching, publish-before-mark, failure behavior, and reruns. |
| [main.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/cmd/catalog/main.go) | Register the new subcommand. |
| [reemit_test.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/cmd/catalog/reemit_test.go) | Extend the existing subcommand-registration assertion. Existing `reemit-policies` behavior stays separate. |
| [server_test.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go) | Keep `fakeStore.CreatePerformance` faithful by copying the bound fake map’s rule setting into the new performance field. No production API or OpenAPI change. |
| [catalog_publication_test.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/smoke/catalog_publication_test.go) | Add the enabled-v1/bound-version/schema-5/adjacency smoke case. Keep `TestSeatedPublicationCoexistsWithGA` as the rule-off schema-4 plus GA proof. |
| `smoke/catalog_orphan_correction_test.go` — **new** | Seed the historical schema-4 state, run the real command twice, and prove inventory upgrade plus projection. |
| [ADR-041](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/docs/adr/ADR-041-orphan-seat-arbitration.md) | Record that TKT-183 chose the “drain old producer replicas first” branch. |
| [development.md](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/docs/development.md) | Add the operator command, rollout order, drain precondition, expected counts, rerun behavior, and honest-writer boundary. |

No OpenAPI or generated files need changing. No inventory production or test files need changing for AC7.

## 3. Test plan

The first red test should be the new `TestWireGoldenPerformancePublishedSchema5OrphanPrevention` in `wire_compat_test.go`. After adding only the new `Performance` field as test scaffolding, it will receive schema 4 without the flag instead of the exact expected schema-5 bytes. Then implement the fork. The existing schema-4 golden must remain untouched in that same commit.

| AC | Test seam |
|---|---|
| 1 | Extend existing `TestPerformancePublishedEnvelopeSchemas`; add new `TestSeatedPublicationEnvelopeSchema5` in `events_test.go`; add the schema-5 wire golden. |
| 2 | Existing `TestWireGoldenPerformancePublishedSchema4Seated`, schema-2 and schema-3 goldens remain unchanged. Existing `TestSeatedPublicationCoexistsWithGA` continues proving rule-off schema 4 and GA schema 2 through the stack. |
| 3 | New schema-5 literal beside the unchanged schema-4 literal in `wire_compat_test.go`. These goldens are inline; there are no separate golden fixture files. |
| 4 | New smoke test in `catalog_publication_test.go`: publish enabled v1, bind the performance, edit the family to published v2 with rule off and different geometry, then publish the performance. Assert schema 5, v1 ID, flag true, and v1’s projection. |
| 5 | The same smoke test waits for `inventory_pools.orphan_prevention_enabled=true` and asserts the exact reciprocal rows in `seat_claim_adjacency`, including the middle seat’s two neighbours. |
| 6 | New identity tests prove the correction ID is deterministic and distinct from `EventID` and `BackfillEventID`. Store smoke proves only historical enabled bindings with an unset correction marker are selected. Command tests prove publication precedes marking. |
| 7 | Already covered by existing `TestProvisionSeatedUpgradesAnExistingPool`, `TestProvisionSeatedRuleFlagIsMonotonic`, and `TestProvisionSeatedRefusesToAdoptAMismatchedPool`. No new inventory scope. |
| 8 | New command test runs the runner twice: first run publishes/marks candidates; second returns zero candidates. E2E smoke also invokes the CLI twice and asserts one pool, unchanged adjacency cardinality, and one consumed correction identity. |
| 9 | New `catalog_orphan_correction_test.go` creates an enabled published map/performance, simulates its historical schema-4 publication, waits for the ordinary seated pool, runs the wave, and proves flag plus projection. |

Additional adversarial command tests:

- Publish failure does not mark the candidate.
- Mark failure aborts; rerun republishes the same deterministic identity.
- Multiple pages drain in UUID-keyset order.
- Rule-off, GA, unpublished, unacknowledged, and already-corrected rows are excluded.
- Concurrent runners may duplicate the broker call but cannot create distinct identities or duplicate inventory effects.

## 4. Correction-wave design

### Identity

Add a new fixed epoch and derivation, proposed as:

- `orphanPreventionCorrectionEpoch = "orphan-prevention-schema5-1"` — **new**
- `OrphanPreventionCorrectionEventID(perf)` — **new**
- SHA-1 UUID namespace key:  
  `subject + ":correction:" + epoch + ":" + performance_id + ":" + published_at`

The ID is:

- distinct from live `EventID`;
- distinct from the existing re-entry `BackfillEventID`;
- stable across crashes and reruns;
- scoped to one performance publication.

`backfillEpoch` must not be bumped. Doing so would change `reemit-policies` identities for every ungrouped slot and still risks using an identity already consumed as schema 4. This wave needs its own semantic namespace and candidate set.

### Durable progress

The new nullable `orphan_prevention_emitted_at` is the schema-5 coverage marker.

- Old catalog binaries continue setting only `event_emitted_at`.
- New live schema-5 publication sets both markers after broker acknowledgement.
- The correction query selects performances with:
  - `published_at IS NOT NULL`;
  - `event_emitted_at IS NOT NULL`;
  - exact bound `seat_maps.orphan_prevention_enabled = true`;
  - `orphan_prevention_emitted_at IS NULL`.
- The runner publishes schema 5, then marks the row.
- A crash between those operations causes a rerun under the same identity.
- No marker is written before a successful JetStream acknowledgement.

The read should join the seat-map version in `performanceFrom`, not perform a second lookup. That gives every emission path—ordinary publication, owed publication during archive/closure, series transitions, and correction—the flag from the exact bound row in the same hydrated read. It avoids an N+1 correction scan and makes accidentally resolving the family’s current version much harder.

### Where it runs

Use a new catalog CLI subcommand:

```text
catalog reemit-orphan-prevention
```

Operationally:

```text
docker compose exec catalog /app reemit-orphan-prevention
```

Smoke can follow the existing `reemit-policies` precedent and run the catalog image with `docker run --rm` on the smoke network.

It should not be an automatic Compose startup job. Startup ordering only proves that one new container is healthy; it does not prove every old catalog replica in a rolling deployment has drained.

### Rolling-deployment race

I choose ADR-041’s explicit drain option.

Required rollout:

1. Confirm TKT-181 inventory and TKT-182 enforcement are fully deployed.
2. Run catalog migration 0015 out-of-band.
3. Roll out the TKT-183 catalog binary.
4. Verify every schema-4-producing catalog replica is terminated/drained.
5. Run `reemit-orphan-prevention`.
6. Run it again; expect zero remaining candidates.

This is the only honest finite one-shot design available with the repository’s current infrastructure. A command that merely loops until one empty scan still has a final race: an old replica can publish immediately after the empty scan. A watermark also cannot classify a later old-writer publication unless old writers participate in the protocol. There is no deployment registry or producer-version lease in the repository.

## 5. Risks and open decisions

- **Human/deployment decision:** Can the real deployment process positively attest that all old catalog replicas have drained? If not, the chosen design is insufficient. Scope would need to expand to a persistent correction outbox/worker or a database-backed producer-generation fence that old writers cannot bypass.
- **Rollback:** Rolling catalog back to the schema-4 producer after the wave recreates the same gap for newly published enabled performances. The runbook must treat producer rollback as requiring another new rollout, drain, and rerun.
- **Marker correctness:** `orphan_prevention_emitted_at` is application-owned evidence, not tamper-evidence. A catalog DB writer can set or clear it, change bindings, or forge candidates.
- **NATS dedup duration:** Broker dedup is not the long-term guarantee. Durable consumer `consumed_events` plus the deterministic correction ID provides convergence after the broker’s duplicate window expires.
- **Existing `reemit-policies`:** After the forward schema fork, it may serialize an enabled seated performance as schema 5 because it shares the live envelope builder. That is safe but cannot replace this wave: its fixed IDs may already have been consumed as schema 4.
- **Archive overlap:** Including historically published/acknowledged candidates may correct an already-archived pool. `ProvisionSeated` only turns on the flag/adds adjacency; it does not reopen the pool, so this is safe and satisfies the literal “already-published” scope.

No acceptance criterion appears technically unachievable, but the rolling-race guarantee is conditional on the drain attestation above.

## 6. AC7: definitive answer

Yes—TKT-181 already satisfies AC7.

[ProvisionSeated](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/inventory/internal/store/seat_claims.go:340) inserts the fresh correction ID into `consumed_events`, locks an existing pool, verifies that its kind, organizer, and exact `seat_map_id` match, monotonically updates `orphan_prevention_enabled` to true, inserts the validated adjacency, and commits all effects atomically.

The existing [TestProvisionSeatedUpgradesAnExistingPool](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/inventory/internal/store/seat_occupancy_smoke_test.go:731) starts with a schema-4-style rule-off seated pool without projection and proves the fresh schema-5 event upgrades it to flag-on with adjacency. The neighboring monotonicity and mismatch tests close stale replay and wrong-pool adoption risks.

Therefore: drop inventory implementation changes from TKT-183.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-review -->
## Plan critique — TKT-183 (by **main-agent**, cross-model against gpt-5.6-sol's draft)

### Seam verification — clean

Every file, symbol and test the draft names exists at HEAD. Checked individually: `performanceColumns`, `performanceFrom`, `scanPerformance`, `MarkPerformanceEventEmitted` (postgres.go); `TestPerformancePublishedEnvelopeSchemas`, `TestWireGoldenPerformancePublishedSchema4Seated` (internal/events); `TestSeatedPublicationCoexistsWithGA` (smoke/catalog_publication_test.go); `TestProvisionSeatedUpgradesAnExistingPool` (inventory); `reemit-policies` registered in `main.go`; latest catalog migration is `0014`. **No hallucinated seams** — the failure mode a drafter that cannot run the gate usually exhibits did not occur.

### ✅ Accept — AC7 is already satisfied, drop it

Confirmed independently. `ProvisionSeated` inserts the event id into `consumed_events` with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and **returns early on conflict**, then on the existing-pool branch verifies kind/organizer/exact `seat_map_id`, upgrades `orphan_prevention_enabled` monotonically, and writes the adjacency in the same transaction. Upgrade-in-place works; a **fresh identity is what makes it reachable**. No inventory changes.

### ❌ Reject — the `orphan_prevention_emitted_at` column and migration 0015

This is the draft's largest piece of scope and it buys nothing the deterministic identity does not already buy.

Replay-safety and idempotency come from the identity, not from a marker: re-running re-emits the **same** id, inventory's `consumed_events` conflict makes it a no-op, and JetStream's `Nats-Msg-Id` window drops the exact republish at the stream. AC8 ("proven by running it twice") is satisfied by asserting one pool, unchanged adjacency and one consumed identity — which is what the draft's own test already asserts.

What the marker adds is a *smaller candidate set on re-runs*. What it costs is a migration, a new column on a hot table, a semantic change to `MarkPerformanceEventEmitted`, and a second source of truth about whether a performance has been corrected — one that can disagree with inventory's actual state. **A row in catalog that says "corrected" while inventory's pool has no projection is worse than no row at all**, and nothing keeps them in step.

Also rejected as a consequence: the `MarkPerformanceEventEmitted` change and `orphan_correction_smoke_test.go`'s marker assertions.

### 🔁 Amend — the drain argument is half right, and the better half is a consequence of the rejection above

The draft chose ADR-041's "drain first" branch and argued a repeat-until-empty reconciliation still races. That is correct **given a marker**. Without one, the shape changes: **every run corrects everything currently bound to an enabled map**, so a late schema-4 publication by an undrained old replica is repaired by *the next run* rather than being permanently invisible. The wave is not a one-shot with a race window; it is a **reconciliation that is safe to re-run indefinitely**, and drain is the operator's *stopping* condition rather than a correctness precondition.

That is a materially stronger position than the draft's, and it is only available because the marker was dropped. ADR-041 records this wording, not "drain-only".

### 🔁 Amend — the fork invariant needs its negative half tested

`omitempty` on a `bool` means a schema-5 payload can never carry `false` — correct and deliberate, and it is what keeps the schema-4 bytes identical. But it makes two failure modes silent:

- schema 5 emitted with the flag **absent** (inventory would provision a rule-enabled pool that says nothing is enabled);
- schema 4 emitted for a bound version that **is** enabled (the exact TKT-179 gap this ticket exists to close, reintroduced).

The draft tests the positive direction only. Both negatives get a test: **schema and flag are the same fact and neither may appear without the other.**

### 🔎 Gap the draft missed — `reemit-policies` inherits the fork

`reemitPolicies` publishes through `PerformancePublishedBackfill`, which shares `performancePublishedEnvelopeWithID`. The moment the fork lands, **`reemit-policies` starts emitting schema 5** for enabled seated slots, under the *backfill* identity — an identity inventory has never consumed, so it will provision/upgrade from it. That is not harmful, but it is an unintended behaviour change to a shipped operator command, and its golden is schema 2 so nothing catches it. It is not in the draft's file list.

Pin it with a test that states what `reemit-policies` now does for an enabled seated slot. Do not try to suppress it — suppression would mean the re-entry backfill emits a payload that disagrees with the live one, which is the exact property TKT-96's golden exists to prevent.

### Pre-mortem

The realistic way this ticket goes wrong is **deployment order**, not code: schema 5 reaching an inventory replica that predates TKT-181 gets quarantined and acked, latches the consumer unready, and needs `reprocess-quarantine` **plus a restart** by an operator. Nothing in the diff can prevent that; only the rollout order can, which is why this ticket exists as its own revision. `docs/development.md` must carry the order as an operator instruction, not as prose.

Second: the LEFT JOIN into the shared read path touches every full-row performance read. It is one join on a primary key and it is what makes AC4 (bound version, never the family's current) true by construction rather than by discipline — accepted, but the column order in `performanceColumns` is documented as load-bearing against `scanPerformance`, so the new column goes at the end.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
## Plan final — TKT-183 (delta on the draft; Gate 2 self-resolved)

**The `kind=plan` draft, as amended below, is the plan.**

### Decisions I made, and why

Gate 2 was waived for this run, so the open decisions are resolved here by me. The rule I applied: prefer what the critique recommends; where it recommends nothing, take the most reversible option.

1. **No migration, no `orphan_prevention_emitted_at`.** (Critique's rejection.) The deterministic identity already delivers replay-safety; a marker adds a second source of truth that can disagree with inventory's real state. *Most reversible:* adding the column later is easy, removing a shipped column that operators have started reading is not.
2. **The wave is a re-runnable reconciliation, drain is the stopping condition.** Follows from (1). Recorded in ADR-041 in those words.
3. **AC7 dropped** — TKT-181's `ProvisionSeated` already upgrades an existing pool; verified independently by both models. No inventory changes in this ticket.
4. **`reemit-policies` inheriting the fork is accepted and pinned by a test, not suppressed.** Suppressing it would make the backfill payload disagree with the live one — the exact property TKT-96's golden exists to prevent. *Most reversible:* a test that states current behaviour can be changed; a divergence baked into two publish paths cannot easily be undone.
5. **The new column goes last in `performanceColumns`.** Its order is documented as load-bearing against `scanPerformance`.

### Amended file list

Dropped from the draft: `migrations/0015_*.sql`, the `MarkPerformanceEventEmitted` change, and the marker assertions in the store smoke test.

Added: a test pinning `reemit-policies`' behaviour for an enabled seated slot.

Everything else stands as drafted.

### Amended test plan

First red test unchanged: the new schema-5 wire golden in `wire_compat_test.go`.

Added to the draft's table:

| AC | Seam |
|---|---|
| 1 (negative half) | schema 5 **never** without the flag; schema 4 **never** for an enabled bound version — schema and flag are one fact |
| — | `reemit-policies` for an enabled seated slot: pinned, not suppressed |
| 8 | one pool, unchanged adjacency cardinality, one consumed identity after two runs — no marker involved |

### Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

The cross-model guarantee covers the draft and it will cover the code, but not the critique's own inventions. These reached this point reviewed only by their author:

1. **Dropping the marker/migration entirely**, and the claim that identity-based idempotency fully covers AC8.
2. **The re-runnable-reconciliation framing** of the deployment race, which is the ADR-041 amendment this ticket will write.
3. **The negative-half fork tests** (schema without flag, flag without schema).
4. **The `reemit-policies` inheritance finding** and the decision to pin rather than suppress.

Items 1 and 2 are the load-bearing ones: if the identity argument is wrong, the wave is not idempotent and the ADR amendment is wrong with it. Both are stated so ai-review can attack them directly — that is where they get their second model.

<!-- sdlc:stage=building kind=ai-review -->
## ai-review pass 1 — **approve**, no material findings (gpt-5.6-sol, adversarial, branch vs main)

Six attack surfaces were named for it, chosen to include the two decisions the plan-final flagged as **introduced at plan-review and reviewed by no second model**. Its verdict on each:

| Focus | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Can schema 5 ever be emitted without the flag, or schema 4 for an enabled version, through *any* path (live publish, owed emission on archive/closure, `reemit-policies`, the wave)? | All production emission paths converge on the shared builder — the fork cannot be bypassed |
| Does the `LEFT JOIN` on `p.seat_map_id` change any existing read's behaviour or row count, and does it follow the bound version rather than the family? | Exact-version hydration preserves row cardinality |
| **Is identity-based convergence sufficient with no correction state?** (plan-review invention #1) | Selection and deterministic identity support the stateless convergence model |

### Read in this order

### The two goldens are the review

`wire_compat_test.go` now holds a schema-5 literal directly beside the untouched schema-4 one. If a future change moves both, it was a rewrite and the rule-off wire contract broke — which is invisible when either golden is read alone. That is the pair's entire job.

### The decision worth arguing with

The draft plan proposed a migration adding `performances.orphan_prevention_emitted_at` as correction state. I rejected it at plan review and shipped a **stateless** wave. The argument: correction state is a second source of truth about something only *inventory* can confirm, and a catalog row reading "corrected" while the pool has no projection is worse than no row — it stops an operator looking.

The consequence is the better half: with no state, every run reconciles the full current candidate set, so ADR-041's rolling-deployment race becomes a **stopping condition** rather than a window. A slot published at schema 4 by an undrained old replica is picked up by the next run. Both the decision and this framing were flagged in `kind=plan-final` as having no second model; ai-review was pointed at them explicitly and cleared them.

`reemit-policies` shares the envelope builder, so it now emits schema 5 for enabled seated slots under the *backfill* identity. Not in the draft's file list; its golden is schema 2, so nothing would have caught it. Pinned by a test rather than suppressed — suppression would make the re_entry backfill disagree with the live payload, the exact property TKT-96's golden prevents.

### Scope dropped, with proof

AC7 (inventory upgrading an existing pool) was already delivered by TKT-181. Both models verified `ProvisionSeated` independently: it locks the row, verifies kind/organizer/exact `seat_map_id`, upgrades the flag monotonically, writes adjacency in the same transaction, and returns early on a consumed event — which is *why* a fresh identity is what makes the upgrade reachable. No inventory changes.

**The correction wave is not exercised against the live stack.** Its target state — published at schema 4 while bound to an enabled version — **cannot be created through the public API**, because a published seat-map version is immutable and the rule cannot be flipped on one. It exists only on databases where TKT-179 shipped before TKT-183. Coverage is the candidate predicate against real Postgres plus the runner's pagination, failure and re-run tests. ### Retro

**The plan critique paid for itself more than the code review did.** Review found nothing; the critique deleted a migration, a column, a semantic change to `MarkPerformanceEventEmitted`, and a whole class of catalog-vs-inventory disagreement — and found a behaviour change to a shipped command (`reemit-policies` inheriting the fork) that the draft had not listed as a file to touch. On this ticket the cheapest defect removal happened before any code existed.

**Rejecting state produced a better guarantee, not a weaker one.** The marker would have made the wave a one-shot with a race window. Without it, every run is a full reconciliation, so drain becomes a stopping condition. That inversion was not visible until the marker was removed — the simplification *was* the design improvement.

**A test scenario too small to show the negative is a test that cannot fail informatively.** The smoke row of three seats made every pair strand the third, so "this selection is allowed" was unprovable there. Same shape as TKT-182's two scenario errors: the rule was right, the fixture was too small to distinguish. Third occurrence in this epic.

**The first clean pass came where the plan was best, not where the code was simplest.** TKT-182's four passes were on a smaller diff than this one.
